title: Windows sign-in fixed — WebAuthn verification now consistent across platforms
summary: A mismatch between client and server WebAuthn settings blocked login on Windows while macOS, iOS, and Android worked fine.
body: The client was requesting `userVerification: "preferred"` while the server required it — on Windows authenticators this mismatch caused authentication to fail silently. Both sides now agree on `required`, so passkey/biometric login works consistently on all platforms. No action needed; the fix is live on self-hosted installs via a normal update.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Self-hosted edition now enforces the 30-CISO / 10-industry caps in code
summary: The free self-hosted build's panel and industry limits are now enforced at runtime, not just described on the pricing page.
body: Previously the OSS build inherited a wider clamp and could silently exceed the documented limits. The caps — 30 CISO panels (fixed) and up to 10 industries — are now checked in code so behaviour matches what the pricing page promises. Cloud and licensed tiers are unaffected.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Fourth panel axis: operating mandate (reactive → embedded → strategic)
summary: CISO personas now vary across a fourth dimension — organisational authority and program maturity — drawn from the CISO-Assembly gap analysis.
body: The new mandate axis distributes personas roughly 40% reactive, 38% embedded, and 22% strategic, independent of the existing risk-appetite, tenure, and sector axes. This closes the most-cited gap from Leg-2 respondents and makes the panel better reflect the full range of how CISOs actually sit within their organisations. Calibration re-run after the change confirmed mean absolute error held steady at ~17.8 pp.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Version number now visible in the app — splash screen and About footer
summary: The running version is shown on the launch splash and in the About footer, single-sourced from the git tag.
body: This was the top piece of in-app feedback from early users. The version line links to the matching GitHub release so you can check the changelog or confirm which patch you're running without leaving the app.
